passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: The remains were described as those of a 9-to-10-year-old Caucasian female who had been shot in the head.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Recovered remains included portions of the skull, rib cage, teeth, jaw, and hair.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Authorities searched Bowman’s mobile home, collecting additional evidence.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Bowman remained outside the continental United States while investigators attempted to determine whether he had any connection to the Short family killings.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Investigators transported bone fragments to Roanoke for DNA analysis.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: The North Carolina medical examiner determined that the child represented by the remains had been shot once in the head.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Investigators awaited DNA confirmation.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Forensic Examination: Preliminary examination indicated the remains belonged to a young female, increasing concern that they could be Jennifer. Dental analysis indicated the remains belonged to a 9-year-old white female. The skull showed evidence of a gunshot wound to the head, consistent with the manner in which Michael and Mary Short had been killed. Investigators stressed that this did not yet constitute a positive identification of Jennifer.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Approximately 20 reporters watched as a line of searchers walked through marshland and investigators used poking sticks in the grass.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Divers searched for approximately five hours.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: They located bones in the water, but the remains proved to be from an animal.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Authorities continued searching for additional portions of the child’s remains and other evidence potentially connected to the homicide.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Search of Pond: Divers searched a pond near the Grogan Road recovery site for additional evidence.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Whitehead said the family had hoped Jennifer would be found alive but that there were “too many coincidences” for him to believe the remains belonged to another child.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: The report noted that authorities had previously determined the remains belonged to a Caucasian girl approximately 9 years old with brown hair, and that there were no other known missing children fitting that description in the immediate region.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Family Member Accepts Remains Are Likely Jennifer’s: James Whitehead, husband of Jennifer’s aunt Carol Whitehead, told The Roanoke Times that he had accepted that the remains were probably Jennifer’s even before DNA confirmation.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Initial DNA testing had not yet produced a conclusive identification, and additional testing continued.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Bowman had left North Carolina shortly after the Short family murders and had been living in the Northwest Territories.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Garrison “Gary” Bowman was arrested by the Royal Canadian Mounted Police in Inuvik, Northwest Territories, Canada, after an incident involving alleged impaired driving. Canadian authorities subsequently held Bowman on an immigration violation.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: The NCIC inquiry revealed that the Royal Canadian Mounted Police had arrested the individual investigators wanted to question in connection with the Jennifer Short investigation.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: After learning Bowman was in custody, investigators began making arrangements to travel to Canada to interview him and search his van.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: The DOJ Inspector General later reported that local investigators initially appeared to believe that a North Carolina search warrant could be used to search Bowman’s vehicle in Canada. When the FBI Legal Attaché in Canada learned of the situation, the Legal Attaché attempted to coordinate with the local FBI office and investigators because a North Carolina warrant could not simply be executed in Canada.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Canadian authorities subsequently transferred Bowman from Inuvik to Yellowknife, where he remained in custody while immigration proceedings were conducted.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: According to a later U.S. Department of Justice Office of the Inspector General report, law enforcement investigating Jennifer Short’s murder learned that Bowman was in Canadian custody after a name check was run through the National Crime Information Center (NCIC).

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Late Night: The Virginia Division of Forensic Science laboratory in Roanoke obtained DNA results positively matching the remains to Jennifer Renee Short.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Sheriff Cassell said investigators had cleared up questions concerning Jennifer’s parentage.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Police said there was no doubt Michael Short was Jennifer’s biological father.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Cassell also stated there was no evidence that either Michael or Mary Short was anything other than Jennifer’s biological parent.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Authorities said the clarification was meant to eliminate speculation and let investigators focus on legitimate leads.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Jennifer Identified: Rockingham County Sheriff Sam Page announced that DNA testing conducted by the Virginia Division of Forensic Science laboratory in Roanoke positively identified the skeletal remains recovered in Rockingham County on September 25 as Jennifer Renee Short. Investigators had received the positive DNA results late the previous night. The medical examiner determined that Jennifer had suffered a gunshot wound to the head.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Authorities publicly confirmed that Bowman was in Canadian custody. Rockingham County Sheriff Sam Page emphasized that Bowman had not been identified as a suspect, but investigators considered him an important person they needed to interview.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Bowman’s location had become increasingly significant after Jennifer Short’s remains were discovered in Rockingham County near property associated with him, and investigators recovered evidence during searches of his North Carolina property.
